data.name: Aalim
data.gender_notes: Aalim is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aalim is a respected Arabic name meaning 'scholar' or 'one who possesses deep knowledge'. It is often used to describe Islamic scholars or those devoted to learning religious sciences. The name Aalim carries the meaning “Scholar, Learned Man” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Arabic. Parents who choose Aalim usually hope their child will grow to embody scholar, learned man and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes wisdom, divine knowledge, and commitment to truth. An Aalim is a guiding light in a community, rooted in understanding and compassion.
data.etymology: Aalim belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Scholar, Learned Man.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aalim total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: عالم
in_arabic.long_meaning: الاسم عالم مشتق من الجذر العربي ع ل م، والذي يعني العلم والمعرفة، وهو مصدر للفعل علِمَ، ويتعلق بالشخص الذي يمتلك العلم والمعرفة، والاسم ذکر في القرآن الكريم في سورة الفاتحة

in_urdu.name: عالم
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام عالم عربي gốc سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے علم اور معرفت، اور یہ لفظ علِمَ سے مشتق ہے، جو شخص کو علم و معرفت کا مالک کہتا ہے، اور یہ نام قرآن پاک میں سورہ الفاتحہ میں ذکر ہوا ہے

in_hindi.name: आलिम
in_hindi.long_meaning: नाम आलिम अरबी मूल से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है ज्ञान और संस्कृति, और यह शब्द علिम से व्युत्पन्न है, जो व्यक्ति को ज्ञान और संस्कृति का धारक कहता है, और यह नाम कुरान में सूरा अल्फातिहा में उल्लेख किया गया है

in_pashto.name: عالم
in_pashto.long_meaning: د نوم عالم د عربي ريشې څخه اخستل شوی، چې معنا يې ده پوهې او فرهنګ، او دا शबد د علِم څخه مشتق شوی، چې د چا پوهې او فرهنګ مالک بلل کېږي، او دا نوم په قرآن کریم کې په سورې الفاتحہ کې یاد شوی

in_english.name: Aalim
in_english.long_meaning: The name Aalim is derived from the Arabic root ع ل م, which means knowledge and culture, and is a source of the verb علِمَ, relating to a person who possesses knowledge and culture, and the name is mentioned in the Quran in Surah Al-Fatihah

pronunciation.pashto: د عالم د تلفظ عالِم دی

data.cultural_impact: The name Aalim is highly valued in Islamic culture as it signifies a deep and profound knowledge, often associated with the study of religious texts and sciences. Aalims are held in high regard and have traditionally played an essential role in preserving and passing on the rich Islamic intellectual heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Aalim can be interpreted as a reminder to constantly seek knowledge and wisdom in order to deepen our connection with Allah and lead a more virtuous life. It is also a reflection of the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) hadith, "The seeking of knowledge is obligatory on every Muslim." (Bukhari and Muslim). The name embodies the Islamic concept of lifelong learning and striving for knowledge in the service of Allah.
data.spiritual_symbolism: An 'Aalim' in Islamic context is a learned scholar, possessing deep knowledge and wisdom in religious and secular matters. They are spiritual beacons, guiding others towards the path of truth and righteousness.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Aalim is mentioned in the Hadith as a title of respect for Islamic scholars. The name Aalim carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Aalim was used to refer to learned Islamic scholars who were respected for their knowledge and wisdom.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Aalim remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
